assessment: This study investigates how different sources of genotoxic stress exacerbate proteome instability, leading to the formation of protein aggregates. These effects are in part caused by an impaired chaperone network and can be relieved by the action of small chaperones with anti-amyloidogenic function. This work functionally connects two fields of research: responses to genotoxic stress and protein aggregation, both of which have fundamental implications for cellular stability and homeostasis during aging. Connecting these two fields sheds new light on basic mechanisms of cell stability and has the potential to help design interventions that buffer both DNA damage responses and proteome stability.
